assessment.prompt: Thought experiment: imagine that a magnesium strip reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid inside a rigid, transparent sealed flask. Describe the gas produced, what happens to the total mass of the sealed flask, and one observation consistent with gas production in this reaction.
assessment.expectedAnswer: Hydrogen gas forms. The total mass of the sealed flask stays constant because the atoms remain inside the closed system, including the gas. Bubbles are consistent with gas production here but do not by themselves prove a chemical reaction.

rubric.name: Identifies hydrogen gas
rubric.description: 3 for hydrogen gas; 1 for a gas without identity; 0 for an incorrect or absent gas.

rubric.name: States sealed-flask total mass is constant
rubric.description: 2 for constant total mass; 0 for a different or missing claim.

rubric.name: Explains mass conservation
rubric.description: 3 for matter/atoms remaining inside including the gas; 1 for an incomplete conservation reason; 0 for no valid explanation.

rubric.name: Interprets bubbles in context
rubric.description: 2 for bubbles consistent with gas production here; 1 for noting bubbles only; 0 for no relevant observation. Bubbles alone do not universally prove chemical change.

caps.condition: No valid explanation of conservation of total mass in the sealed flask

cases.authorScript: The bubbles are hydrogen gas. The total mass of the sealed flask stays the same because the gas remains inside and no atoms disappear. The bubbles are consistent with gas forming here.
